target_customer: Mexican households (and later commercial and industrial businesses) that want cheaper electricity with no upfront cost
problem: Mexican electricity was expensive and complicated, and households lacked credit history and cash to buy solar panels outright.
business_model: Solar financing and leasing (later PPAs, financial leases and direct sales) sold through student ambassadors, retail promoters and local installers

founders.name: Jonah Greenberger
prior_employers: Chevron (Director, helped build a renewable energy investment and construction group)
founders.background_notes: TechCrunch (2015-02-25) calls him the sole founder and says he was 28 at the time of the article. Some sources name Pablo Castellanos as a co-founder, but neither the YC page nor the company site says so, so he is not listed.

investors: IFU (Investment Fund for Developing Countries, Denmark)

competitors.name: Envolta
competitors.what: Mexican solar provider that builds and installs its own panels and leases them to customers

technical_complexity.rationale: Credit scoring from government and public data in a cash economy plus financing structures with investors was nontrivial, but the panels and installs came from partners (TechCrunch 2015-02).

defensibility.rationale: Long contracts, a network of student ambassadors and hundreds of installers, and local credit data were hard to copy quickly; panel hardware was commodity.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent absorbed the wedge. By 2023 Bright described itself as the largest financier of distributed solar in Mexico and added commercial and industrial customers in 2022.

market_need_then: TechCrunch (2015-02) reported high and complex Mexican electricity pricing, with unsubsidized summer bills above 4,000 USD, and Bright claimed solar could cut household bills 20 to 50 percent.

branding.domain_note: Company site is thinkbright.mx, not an exact .com.

identity.logo: Not confirmed. An undated design portfolio describes a sun peeking through a solar panel for a company called Bright, but it is not tied to this company.
identity.voice_and_tone: Positioned as democratizing solar access in Mexico (company site)

branding.brand_signature: Pitch line 'Sunrun for the developing world' and a student ambassador sales force
branding.community_and_virality: Press coverage often mentions investor Leonardo DiCaprio and Sunrun and Tesla founders, which drew attention, but no evidence of a fan community or merch.

brand_strength.rationale: Generic English word with no sourced brand assets beyond the student ambassador channel; awareness came mostly from investor names and press.

pivots.to: Added commercial and industrial solar, later batteries (BESS)
pivots.why: Expansion announced in the company's press release; the site now says it is focused on industry.

outcome_analysis: Bright raised a 4 million dollar seed in 2015, built a student ambassador and installer distribution channel in Mexico, and closed a 31.5 million dollar Series C in July 2023 led by IFU. It expanded into commercial and industrial solar in 2022 and now emphasizes industrial clients and batteries, with over 6,000 clients claimed on its site. The founder's energy finance background and a large, expensive electricity market fit helped, and no shutdown or acquisition is reported.
notes: No Series A or Series B was found, though aggregators cite 59 to 60 million total raised over 7 to 12 rounds, so history is partial. Series C size conflicts (31.5M in Business Wire and others, 32M Canary Media, 35.5M LatamList) and lead is given as IFU or SDG Investment Fund. A debt round dated 2025-10 appears only on CB Insights and is unverified. The Series C release itself returned 403 and was read via search snippets and several outlets.
